question_text: Calculate the dimensions of (a) a cube containing 1 mol of copper and (b) a cube containing 1 mol of lead. Give your answer as a tuple: (cube_dimension_copper, cube_dimension_lead).The units of each required answer are (mm, mm), respectively.
response:
## Reasoning

For a cube containing 1 mol of a material, the edge length comes from the molar volume:

$$V_m = \frac{M}{\rho}, \qquad a = V_m^{1/3}$$

where \(M\) is the molar mass and \(\rho\) is the density.

### (a) Copper
- \(M_{\text{Cu}} = 63.546\ \text{g/mol}\)
- \(\rho_{\text{Cu}} = 8.96\ \text{g/cm}^3\)
- \(V_m = 63.546/8.96 = 7.092\ \text{cm}^3\)
- \(a = (7.092)^{1/3} = 1.921\ \text{cm} = 19.2\ \text{mm}\)

### (b) Lead
- \(M_{\text{Pb}} = 207.2\ \text{g/mol}\)
- \(\rho_{\text{Pb}} = 11.34\ \text{g/cm}^3\)
- \(V_m = 207.2/11.34 = 18.27\ \text{cm}^3\)
- \(a = (18.27)^{1/3} = 2.634\ \text{cm} = 26.3\ \text{mm}\)

$$\boxed{(19.2,\ 26.3)}$$
